summary: The Director-General is the chief executive, "charged with the general responsibility for matters affecting the day-to-day running of the service corps". No provision names an office responsible for the safety or security of corps members at national level.

The State governing board is responsible for "arranging and providing accommodation, boarding, transportation, and providing other facilities which are essential for the welfare of members" and for "deploying members of the service corps within the State".

States provide a minimum annual subvention of N500,000 "to enable it cater adequately for the welfare needs of corps members deployed to the State", and facilities including "orientation camps and transportation facilities".
A "member of the service corps" includes a prospective member unless the context requires otherwise, so duties owed to members extend to those travelling to camp.
The service corps ensures "that as far as possible, Nigerian youths are assigned to jobs in States other than their States of origin".

The Directorate "shall determine the place and time each person ... shall be deployed" and "shall not be compelled in any manner whatsoever to deploy a member ... to any particular undertaking or project". No security criterion for placement is stated; section 9(4) lists qualifications, vacancies and priorities of national needs.

Exemption by Gazette order, and deferment or change of the service period "on being satisfied that there is reasonable cause", each with prior approval of the National Defence and Security Council. Security risk is not named as a ground.
A person aggrieved by a Directorate decision may appeal to the Presidency before going to court.

The Local Government Committee arranges "for the collection of corps members at the end of the orientation course and return them for purposes of the winding-up exercise". The journey from home to camp is not covered.

document: Director-General's address to corps members (2021 Batch B Stream One)
summary: No night travel, including on relocation; shelter at military barracks, NYSC offices, state secretariats or palaces after 6:00 pm; use of recognised motor parks only.
Journeys to end by 6:00 pm; corps members overtaken by darkness to stay at military barracks or other designated places.

Members may not leave the orientation camp, or their station during primary assignment, without the written consent of the principal inspector; under the Second Schedule, a member who leaves the station without consent forfeits the allowance until the case is decided.
State governments provide orientation camps. No standard for camp security is set.

The Local Government Committee has responsibility to "ensure the security of corps members deployed to the local government area"; its members include a representative of the Nigeria Police Force (section 8(2)(c)).
Local governments provide, through the Committee, welfare facilities including transport for inspection, "adequate accommodation" and material for community development service.
Employers provide basic accommodation or N250 a month, welfare facilities "including medical service", and transport or N150 a month.

document: Director-General's address to corps members (2021 Batch B Stream One)
summary: Security consciousness and caution on social media delivered in the closing address of the orientation course.
Members may not ride a motorcycle without a crash helmet during primary assignment. No other safety or security rule appears in the code of conduct.

Grievances go through the head of department or principal inspector, then the State committee chairman, then the Director; a member who "airs his grievance in any news media" is liable to a penalty. No incident reporting procedure is set.

Members who fall ill use the nearest military or government medical facility; private treatment costs may be refunded at the Directorate's discretion. No provision on insurance, compensation or support after violent harm.
The Directorate reports annually to the Presidency by 30 June, and the report is laid before the National Defence and Security Council. No requirement to report incidents or harm to corps members.
Civilian operational leadership of the scheme with the military continuing to provide security support.

Risk-sensitive deployment framework limiting exposure to security flashpoints, especially for non-indigenes in high-risk areas; technology-driven deployment considering state of origin, residence and institution attended.
National grading and certification system for camps covering accommodation, healthcare, safety and infrastructure, with a transition period for state governments.
Attorney-General of the Federation and Federal Ministry of Youth Development directed to amend the NYSC Act; executive bill in preparation as of July 2026.

Refusing a posting to primary assignment is penalised by forfeiture of allowance and an extension of service of double the months out of work on half pay; inducing rejection of a posting carries a 30-day extension on half pay. No exception for security risk is stated.

All communications, including relocation requests, must be endorsed by the corps employer; redress runs from the employer or State Coordinator to the Chairman of the State Governing Board and then the Director-General. No grounds for relocation, and no security ground, are stated.

document: Statements by the Minister of Youth and State Coordinators (2021, 2024, 2026)
summary: Posting to "very unsafe states" stopped (Minister, 2024), Borno postings kept away from areas with security threats (2021), and three Kebbi LGAs excluded from postings (2026). No published criteria or responsible office for these decisions.

The NYSC pledge, signed at swearing-in, commits the member to serve "in any part of the country to which I am deployed and, if need be pay the supreme sacrifice for the fatherland". No provision for risk information or consent.
Members may not travel outside the state of service without written permission of the State Coordinator, including during school and public holidays.

document: Statement by the Minister of Youth (2024)
summary: Group transportation of corps members mentioned as a measure; no procedure published.
Members may not possess firearms or ammunition or bring vehicles or motorcycles into the orientation camp. No camp security standard binds the Directorate or state governments.

document: Statement by the Kebbi State Coordinator (2026)
summary: Kebbi orientation camp moved from Dakingari to Basura, Jega LGA, because of insecurity.

document: NYSC statement on a safety pamphlet (2025)
summary: A safety pamphlet presented to management by a consultant in 2021 "was never adopted as an official policy of the Scheme"; no adopted security guidance is described.
Members may not address the press on any policy issue without written consent of the State Coordinator; penalty of 30 days' extension of service on half pay.

document: NYSC statements after the Kogi abduction (2026)
summary: Rescue of corps members abducted on 26 August 2026 was carried out by the armed forces, police, Department of State Services and vigilante groups; NYSC stated that protocols would be reviewed. No NYSC crisis or kidnap response plan is cited.

Health and life insurance for every corps member since 2004, starting from issue of the call-up letter; medical claims through the National Health Insurance Authority. Insurer and cover limits not published.
An Assistant Director (Insurance) at NYSC headquarters presented a N1 million death benefit to the family of a prospective corps member killed on the way to camp.
Medical care at military or government facilities; private treatment refunded at the Director-General's discretion.

document: NYSC statements after the Kogi abduction (2026)
summary: NYSC stated that "lessons had been learnt" and that protocols would be reviewed; no review report or schedule published.
"Risk-sensitive deployment to better protect corps members" implies an assessment of risk, but no method, data source or responsible office is announced.
"Improved camp standards through a national grading and certification system"; the certifying office is not named.
